title: Battery storage request, speed pilot, heritage approvals
subtitle: Pedestrian easement, GRCA agreement, hybrid meeting rules, radio purchase, GOST bus licence and deferred 2024 meeting schedule.
overview: Council referred a request for municipal support of a proposed Elora battery energy storage project to staff for a report {{vote:m5}}. The developer said the support resolution would be part of its provincial bid, which is due December 12, 2023, so timing matters. Council has not yet decided whether to give support.

Council approved the Committee of the Whole report {{vote:m6}}. It includes a pilot of 40 km/h speed limits in an urban neighbourhood with community consultation, and a new controlled pedestrian crossing on St. David Street North at St. George Street. It also approves a Memorandum of Understanding with the Grand River Conservation Authority and repeals the Township's demolition control by-law. After a closed session, Council supported obtaining a public pedestrian easement over Conservation Authority land {{vote:m3}}.

Council also approved a partial demolition at a listed Elora property, two heritage permits, a single-source radio purchase for emergency communications, a licence agreement for the GOST bus service, and hybrid meeting rules. A decision on the 2024 meeting schedule was deferred so staff can explain the proposed changes {{vote:m15}}.

decisions.detail: Council referred the developer's request for a municipal support resolution to staff for a report.

Council approved the report, including a 40 km/h speed limit pilot, a new St. David Street North pedestrian crossing, a Grand River Conservation Authority agreement, and repeal of the demolition control by-law.

decisions.item: Pedestrian easement from Grand River Conservation Authority
decisions.detail: Council supported obtaining a public pedestrian easement over Conservation Authority land and delegated the Managing Director of Planning and Development to complete it.
Council approved demolition of only the rear two-storey addition, with the property staying on the Municipal Heritage Register as a listed property.
Council named MRC Wireless vendor of record and authorized a single-source purchase of 151 radios and 43 microphones for $170,755.32.
Council authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the licence agreement with the City of Owen Sound for the Guelph Owen Sound Transportation service.
Council authorized a procedure by-law amendment and adopted a Hybrid Electronic Meeting Policy for Council and committee meetings.
Council deferred the draft 2024 Council and Committee meeting schedule so staff can provide more detail on the merits of the proposed changes.
